title: Finger Paisley Mehndi Design for Finger
descriptionParagraphs: Look at the sunburst first, then the geometric grid that frames it. This one is made for the fingers and is on the harder side. Wear it for Eid.

Finger designs are quick to apply and dry fast, which makes them practical when time is short. Fingertips have thicker skin, so the stain there usually develops darker than on the rest of the hand. This pattern needs steady pressure control and fine line work, so it is best attempted after practising simpler designs.
Ring-style bands drawn around one or more fingers imitate jewelry and pair well with a bare palm. Fingertips have thick skin, so they usually take the darkest stain on the hand.
Application tips: The stain starts orange and darkens to reddish brown over 24 to 48 hours as it oxidises. Wash and dry the skin before application and skip lotion or oil, which block the dye.

image.alt: Finger Paisley mehndi design for finger henna pattern

faq.q: How long does a mehndi stain last?
faq.a: A natural henna stain usually lasts one to three weeks. It fades faster on areas that are washed or rubbed often, such as the hands.

faq.q: How long should I leave the mehndi paste on?
faq.a: Keep the paste on for at least four to six hours. Many people leave it overnight for a darker stain.

faq.q: Why does my mehndi look orange at first?
faq.a: Fresh henna stains are orange. The colour deepens to reddish brown over the next 24 to 48 hours as the dye oxidises.

title: Finger Wave Pattern Mehndi Design for Back Hand
descriptionParagraphs: Look at the circular medallion first, then the petal arrangement that frames it. This one is made for the back of the hand and is on the harder side. Wear it for everyday wear.

Skin on the back of the hand is thinner than the palm, so the stain is usually lighter and fades sooner. Leaving the paste on for longer helps the colour develop. This pattern needs steady pressure control and fine line work, so it is best attempted after practising simpler designs.

Finger-only mehndi is a popular minimal choice for people who want a small design that is quick to apply. Filling the fingertips solid with henna is a traditional look in many regions, from South Asia to North Africa.
Application tips: Keeping the skin warm while the paste is on helps the colour develop. Keep the fingers slightly apart while the paste dries so neighbouring designs do not touch.

faq.a: Natural henna is never black. Products sold as black henna often contain PPD, a hair-dye chemical that can cause skin reactions, so they are best avoided.

title: Finger Geometric Grid Mehndi Design for Back Hand
descriptionParagraphs: A finger pattern for the back of the hand, built from teardrop cascade and peacock motif. Difficulty: medium. Good for a party.

Skin on the back of the hand is thinner than the palm, so the stain is usually lighter and fades sooner. Leaving the paste on for longer helps the colour develop. This pattern suits someone who is already comfortable with basic lines, dots and petals and wants to practise even spacing.

title: Finger Bell Garland Mehndi Design for Foot
descriptionParagraphs: Made for the foot, this finger design mixes bracelet cuff with floral vine. It's a medium-level design. Many people pick a design like this for Eid.

The soles take henna as well as the palms do, while the top of the foot stains lighter. Stay seated and avoid walking until the paste has dried completely. This pattern suits someone who is already comfortable with basic lines, dots and petals and wants to practise even spacing.

Finger-only mehndi is a popular minimal choice for people who want a small design that is quick to apply. Filling the fingertips solid with henna is a traditional look in many regions, from South Asia to North Africa.

Application tips: Leave the paste on for at least four to six hours; the longer it stays, the deeper the stain. Dab a lemon and sugar mixture on the dried paste to keep it moist and stuck to the skin.

faq.a: Natural henna is never black. Products sold as black henna often contain PPD, a hair-dye chemical that can cause skin reactions, so they are best avoided.

faq.q: Should I do a patch test before applying mehndi?
faq.a: Yes. Apply a small amount of the paste to the inner arm and wait 24 hours, especially if you have sensitive skin or are using a new cone.

title: Finger Swirl Mehndi Design for Full Hand
descriptionParagraphs: Made for the full hand, this finger design mixes wave pattern with sunburst. It's on the harder side. Many people pick a design like this for Diwali.

Full-hand designs run from the fingertips to the wrist, so allow extra time for application. Work from the wrist towards the fingers, or the other way round, so you never rest on wet paste. This pattern needs steady pressure control and fine line work, so it is best attempted after practising simpler designs.
Ring-style bands drawn around one or more fingers imitate jewelry and pair well with a bare palm. Fingertips have thick skin, so they usually take the darkest stain on the hand.

Application tips: Scrape the dried paste off instead of washing it, and keep the area away from water for the first 12 to 24 hours. The stain starts orange and darkens to reddish brown over 24 to 48 hours as it oxidises.
